newsitem.title: RUSSIA: BOXING-RUSSIAN OLYMPIC SQUAD BOXER KNIFED TO DEATH.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-RUSSIAN OLYMPIC SQUAD BOXER KNIFED TO DEATH.

text.p: Eduard Zakharov, a boxer in the 1996 Russian Olympic team, died from multiple stab wounds on Tuesday night in his flat in the Siberian town of Ukhta, Itar-Tass news agency said on Wednesday, quoting police sources.
Police said Zakharov had a quarrel at home with two men. His wife ran for help, but she returned to find the 23-year-old boxer bleeding on the floor with at least ten knife wounds.
He died minutes later. The police said two suspects had been detained, but the reasons for the killing were not known.
Officials at the Russian Boxing Federation confirmed that Zakharov had been killed, but said they knew no details.

Zakharov joined Russia's junior squad in 1988. In 1994 he won the Russian Boxing Championship and represented Russia at the Atlanta Olympic Games in 1996, where he reached the quarter-final stage in the light-welterweight category.
It was the second mysterious death of a Russian sporting figure in recent weeks.

Last month's contract killing of the head of the Russian Ice Hockey Federation Valentin Sych sent shock waves through the sports establishment, raising international concern over criminal involvement in Russian sports.
Links between crime and sport in Russia range from much rumoured but seldom proved match-rigging to attempts to take control of sports clubs and organisations.
Many sports organisations, given tax exemptions by the state to help cash-starved clubs, became prime targets for criminals who used them to launder money and send it out of the country.
